final_24.first_experiment: Three-party command, warranty, and finance-rights gate (4 months; $45,000). Pre-register: Freeze variables, command authority, warranty consequence, data rights, minimum $25,000 follow-on funding, and no-credit rule for generic lender interest. Pass: Three-party signed term sheet grants command authority; Logged variables explicitly affect warranty or financing; At least $25,000 follow-on funding. Kill: OEM controller remains sole authority; Lender accepts only OEM/EPC guarantees; No data rights or funding. Budget: warranty and command matrix $8,000, oem developer workshops $10,000, lender technical adviser $8,000, legal and data rights $8,000, term sheet negotiation $5,000, controller mockup $3,000, independent review $2,000, contingency $1,000.
final_24.first_experiment_decisive_basis: Without contractual command and recognition, the device cannot exist as proposed. The test directly kills that premise.
final_24.selection_rationale: Selected only after literal gate adjudication and portfolio constraint solving; the score retains competition, access, timing, and evidence uncertainty rather than treating structural fit as proof.

final_24.timing_window: Component-margin business with entrenched incumbents; if HVDC protection stays vertically bundled inside converter OEMs, merchant sensing stays niche.
final_24.first_experiment: Unbundled wideband-sensor socket test (6 months; $35,000). Pre-register: Freeze DC-to-100 kHz requirement, incumbent baseline request, six targets, unbundled interface, and paid NRE threshold. Kill: All buyers require proprietary station package; No paid evaluation; No buyer-valued bandwidth/accuracy gap. final_24.first_experiment_decisive_basis: The merchant socket, not 1 kA lab feasibility, is load-bearing and can be killed cheaply.

final_24.concept: High-speed permanent-magnet turbo-generator + power-converter 'electrical cartridge' (0.3-20 MW) for waste-heat sCO2 and geothermal/ORC power blocks
final_24.timing_window: If sCO2 retrofit demand stays CNNC-internal and ORC incumbents keep generators in-house, the merchant socket is small; mitigated by multi-cycle applicability and the documented turbine capacity shortage.
final_24.first_experiment: Electrical-cartridge OEM socket test (4 months; $68,000). Pre-register: Freeze one narrow rating, price, warranty, service scope, eight OEMs, minimum $150,000 co-development, and no-credit rules for integrated end-customer orders. Pass: Two unrelated OEMs externalize the same electrical island; One commits >=$150,000 paid NRE or purchase; Interface excludes incumbent-integrated cases. Kill: Fewer than two externalize; No paid commitment; Only complete-turbine vendors show demand. Budget: interface and rating specification $12,000, oem workshops $16,000, make buy and warranty model $10,000, lifecycle cost model $8,000, export and standards $6,000, paid nre negotiation $8,000, independent review $4,000, contingency $4,000.
final_24.first_experiment_decisive_basis: The merchant socket is contradicted by current transactions; this test resolves it before an unaffordable rig.
final_24.selection_rationale: Selected only after literal gate adjudication and portfolio constraint solving; the score retains competition, access, timing, and evidence uncertainty rather than treating structural fit as proof.
